body.x: E-POWERTRAIN KOREA (CEO Lee Euichun) will participate in CES 2025 from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, USA, as part of the K-Startup Pavilion.

The company specializes in designing high-performance electric propulsion systems for electric vehicles (EVs), advanced air mobility (AAM/UAM), and electric maritime systems (e-Ships). Known for its proprietary design capabilities, its flagship product, the UE-Series electric engine, showcases its proven expertise and draws significant industry attention.

At CES 2025, E-POWERTRAIN KOREA will highlight the cutting-edge UE-Series, aiming to establish connections with global unmanned aircraft manufacturers. The engine meets U.S. Department of Defense standards (MIL-STD Capabilities, ADS) and delivers over 25kW/kg of power and 70Nm/kg of torque, setting a benchmark for quality and performance.

The UE-Series has demonstrated superior energy efficiency, verified by KOLAS testing, and leverages its patented ‘Yokeless Dual Magnet’ technology. This gives the engine an edge over competitors like GE and Siemens, making it particularly suitable for unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft.

An E-POWERTRAIN KOREA spokesperson explained, “The UE-Series achieves thrust-to-weight ratios four times higher than first-generation motors and excels in thermal performance and heat resistance during operation. Furthermore, its design allows for direct propeller drive without a transmission, significantly reducing the weight of propulsion systems. This makes it a compelling choice for global companies competing in the UAM and unmanned aircraft mobility sectors.”

The company also emphasized its ongoing efforts to develop next-generation electric engines for the defense industry, secure electric propulsion technology for global mobility companies, and obtain international technical certifications. “We plan to showcase these achievements and our future product pipeline at CES 2025, aiming to expand into markets in the U.S. and beyond,” the spokesperson added.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
